definition: GitHub Copilot is a code completion and programming AI-assistant developed by GitHub and OpenAI that assists users of Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Neovim, Eclipse and JetBrains integrated development environments (IDEs) by autocompleting code.
details: Currently available by subscription to individual developers and to businesses, the generative AI software was first announced by GitHub on 29 June 2021. Users can choose the large language model used for generation.

explainer.lead: GitHub Copilot is a subscription-based AI programming assistant from GitHub and OpenAI that suggests code completions inside several popular development tools. It can save programmers some routine typing while leaving them to review and decide what code to keep.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a writing helper that guesses the rest of your sentence as you type. Copilot does something similar for computer code, offering a possible continuation while you work. You can use the suggestion, change it, or ignore it.
tiers.practitioner: Copilot is used for code completion in Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Neovim, Eclipse, and JetBrains IDEs, with subscriptions for individuals and businesses. Users can choose which large language model generates suggestions. Generated code still needs review and testing before it is relied on.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text terms, Copilot maps editor context to a suggested code completion: completion = chosen_LLM(context), with the suggestion presented inside the IDE. It is generative AI software rather than one fixed language model, because the user can select the model. A completion is a candidate output, not a guarantee that the code is correct.

explainer.example: While writing a function in Visual Studio Code, a developer types its name and opening lines. Copilot suggests code for the remaining body; the developer checks the suggestion, edits any unsuitable parts, and then tests the completed function.

usedIn.name: Visual Studio Code
usedIn.detail: Provides AI-assisted code completion while developers edit programs.

usedIn.name: Visual Studio
usedIn.detail: Brings Copilot's autocomplete assistance into Microsoft's IDE.

usedIn.name: Neovim
usedIn.detail: Lets developers receive Copilot code suggestions in this editor.

usedIn.name: Eclipse and JetBrains IDEs
usedIn.detail: Supports code completion across these additional development environments.

explainer.intuition: Copilot treats code writing partly like predictive text: it proposes a continuation based on what is already in the editor. The programmer remains in control of whether the suggestion becomes part of the program.
howItWorks: A developer writes code in a supported IDE.
Copilot takes the current coding context and requests a completion.
The large language model selected by the user generates the suggestion.
The IDE displays the suggested code for the developer to use, modify, or reject.
explainer.whyItMatters: It brings generative AI directly into everyday programming environments, where completions can reduce repetitive typing. Its individual and business subscriptions make the same assistant available to solo developers and organizations.
misconceptions: Copilot is not an IDE itself; it assists users inside supported editors and IDEs.
It is not tied to one unchangeable language model; users can choose the model used for generation.
A suggested completion is not automatically correct or ready to ship.
